title: Coding Set 09: Missing Number & Matrix Diagonals
description: Reported HCL coding rounds: finding the missing and duplicate numbers in 1..N without extra space, and square matrix diagonal difference.

problems.title: Missing Number and Duplicate Element in 1..N
problems.statement: You are given an integer N and an array of N integers where every integer lies between 1 and N inclusive. Exactly one number in 1..N is missing and one number appears twice. Print '<missing> <duplicate>' in O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
problems.inputFormat:
Line 1: Integer N.
Line 2: N space-separated integers.
problems.outputFormat: Two space-separated integers: missing followed by duplicate.

starterCode.python:
import sys

data = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
n = data[0]
a = data[1:1+n]
# Write your solution here

solutions.python:
import sys

data = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
n = data[0]
a = data[1:1+n]
s = sum(a)
sq = sum(x * x for x in a)
es = n * (n + 1) // 2
esq = n * (n + 1) * (2 * n + 1) // 6
diff = es - s
sum_md = (esq - sq) // diff
missing = (diff + sum_md) // 2
dup = missing - diff
print(missing, dup)

edgeCases: Sum of squares up to N=10^5 reaches ~3.3*10^14, so 64-bit `long` (or XOR splitting) is mandatory

problems.title: Square Matrix Diagonal Absolute Difference
problems.statement: Given an N x N square integer matrix M, compute the absolute difference between the sum of its primary diagonal (top-left to bottom-right) and its secondary diagonal (top-right to bottom-left).
problems.inputFormat:
Line 1: Integer N.
Next N lines: N space-separated integers per row.
problems.outputFormat: A single non-negative integer representing |PrimarySum - SecondarySum|.

starterCode.python:
import sys

data = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
n = data[0]
# Write your solution here

solutions.python:
import sys

data = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
n = data[0]
idx = 1
d1 = d2 = 0
for i in range(n):
    for j in range(n):
        v = data[idx]
        idx += 1
        if i == j:
            d1 += v
        if i + j == n - 1:
            d2 += v
print(abs(d1 - d2))

problems.spaceComplexity: O(1) — does not even need to store the N x N matrix in memory.
edgeCases: 1x1 matrix: same cell belongs to both diagonals -> difference is 0
Large values require 64-bit `long` to prevent overflow
